title: The Kindly Room
premise: Ada Voss, a surveyor who has spent her life being unremarkable on purpose, is sent to appraise Hollowmere House, a derelict property whose inventory lists keep rewriting themselves to include her. As the house's mirrors begin lagging a second behind reality, she learns it has been holding seven 'residents' since 1974, when the previous owner's son took something from the house and fled. The house doesn't want to trap Ada; it wants her to belong, and belonging here means never leaving. To free herself and the others, Ada must return the stolen thing—a child's name, spoken aloud and carried away—before the harvest moon rises, choosing at last between safe invisibility and a family that costs everything.
about_author: Quentin Amberdale is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent fifteen years cataloguing empty houses across northern England before turning to horror. Their fiction explores the quiet dread of places that remember their occupants better than the occupants remember themselves.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Ada Voss arrives at Hollowmere House for a routine appraisal, POV hers. She counts rooms, photographs decay, and notes that the 1974 survey file lists eight occupants though the house has been empty for decades. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking her lifelong habit of making herself invisible.

chapters.title: Eight Names
chapters.summary: Ada cross-references county records at the village library, POV hers. Seven residents vanished in October 1974; the eighth name on the house's list is illegible—until she looks again and reads her own. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into the first real fear.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Working overnight in the house, Ada notices every mirror reflects the room a full second behind her movements, POV hers. In one mirror, something moves that she hasn't moved yet. Emotional beat: vertigo—the sense of being watched by herself.

chapters.title: The Kindly Room
chapters.summary: Ada finds a small warm bedroom the floor plans don't include, POV hers. It smells of bread and lavender; a bed is turned down as if expecting her. Emotional beat: horrifying comfort—being wanted by something that shouldn't want anything.

chapters.title: Mrs. Ellery's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the village archive, elderly Mrs. Ellery recognizes the house's address and goes white, POV shifting partly to her memory of 1974. Her brother was one of the seven who stayed. Emotional beat: grief and warning—'the house isn't cruel, that's what makes it worse.'

chapters.title: Doors That Count
chapters.summary: Ada returns to find doors added overnight—a corridor with nine doors where there were eight, POV hers. Each door bears a name; the ninth says VOSS. Emotional beat: claustrophobic inevitability as the house builds her a place.

chapters.title: The Boy in the Wallpaper
chapters.summary: Stripping wallpaper in the east room, Ada uncovers children's drawings beneath: a boy, a small silver object, an open door, POV hers with flashes of the boy's perspective. Emotional beat: pity—the house's hunger began with a theft.

chapters.title: What Thomas Took
chapters.summary: Mrs. Ellery tells the story: in 1974, young Thomas Merrick stole the house's 'hearth-name'—a christening cup engraved with the family name—and ran, POV alternating Ada/Mrs. Ellery. The seven residents who tried to stop him simply never came out. Emotional beat: dawning understanding of the debt.

chapters.title: Reflections Ahead
chapters.summary: The mirrors now show Ada things before they happen: her hand opening a door she hasn't touched, POV hers. She tries to leave; the road loops back to the gate no matter which way she drives. Emotional beat: panic curdling into resignation.

chapters.title: Supper for Nine
chapters.summary: Ada wakes to find the kitchen laid for nine, food still steaming, POV hers. Faint voices thank her for staying. For one terrible moment she almost answers. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging—her loneliness weaponized.

chapters.title: Thomas Merrick, Aged Sixty-One
chapters.summary: Ada tracks Thomas to a care home two counties away, POV hers. He is lucid but terrified, clutching a silver cup he's never been able to throw away. Emotional beat: confrontation with the thief—an old man who has also never belonged anywhere since.

chapters.title: He Won't Go Back
chapters.summary: Thomas refuses to return, insisting the house will take his name and make him one of its residents forever, POV mostly his through Ada's questions. He reveals the cup must be returned by someone the house has already claimed. Emotional beat: despair—the debt can't be paid by proxy.

chapters.title: The Ninth Door Opens
chapters.summary: Back at Hollowmere, Ada's door stands open onto the Kindly Room, now furnished entirely with objects from her own flat, POV hers. Her reflection steps out of the mirror without her. Emotional beat: identity dissolving—the house is finishing her room, and her.

chapters.title: Seven Voices
chapters.summary: At moonrise minus three nights, the seven residents finally appear to Ada—not as monsters but as tired people waiting in the hall, POV shared among them briefly. They explain they stayed because leaving meant the house would starve and take the town instead. Emotional beat: terrible compassion for her captors.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises In Four Days
chapters.summary: Ada researches hearth-names and learns the cup holds the house's original family name; without it the house cannot 'let go' of anyone, POV hers. Returning it won't free the seven—it will erase them. Emotional beat: moral weight—saving them may mean unmaking them.

chapters.title: A Name of One's Own
chapters.summary: Ada confronts why invisibility has always felt safe: a childhood of being passed between relatives, unnamed in every household, POV hers in flashback. She realizes the house exploited a wound she'd hidden even from herself. Emotional beat: painful self-recognition.

chapters.title: Bargaining With Walls
chapters.summary: Ada speaks aloud to the house, offering a trade: her name freely given in exchange for the seven's release, POV hers. The mirrors go still, listening. The Kindly Room's door unlocks. Emotional beat: fragile hope built on sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: On the night before the harvest moon, Ada walks the corridor of nine doors carrying the recovered cup, each resident's door opening as she passes, POV hers. They follow her toward the front hall like a funeral procession. Emotional beat: solemn courage.

chapters.title: What Was Taken in 1974
chapters.summary: Under the rising harvest moon, Ada sets the cup on the hearth—but instead of surrendering her own name, she gives the house a new one, naming it 'Hollowmere, Home,' POV hers with the house responding through light and warmth. Emotional beat: climax—refusing the terms of the bargain and inventing better ones.

chapters.title: Letting Go
chapters.summary: The seven residents fade not into erasure but into release, each thanking her as they go; the mirrors catch up to real time, POV hers. The ninth door becomes a plain closet. Emotional beat: bittersweet triumph and exhaustion.

chapters.title: Appraisal Complete
chapters.summary: Ada files her survey, listing the house honestly: sound roof, nine doors, one room that keeps bread warm, POV hers. She buys Hollowmere rather than condemn it. Emotional beat: claiming belonging on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Lights We Keep On
chapters.summary: Months later, Ada hosts the first of many suppers—Mrs. Ellery, Thomas in his wheelchair, neighbors drawn by rumor of a kindly house, POV hers. One mirror lags a half-second, just enough to feel like company. Emotional beat: found family, chosen and kept, with the door left unlocked.
